svg.aria-label: The exponent component f(n) of the claimed subexponential SAT bound against log10 n
svg.text: f(n) = (ln ln(n+16))² / √ln(n+16), so A·n·f(n) is the exponent in 2^(A·runtimeScale n) of SubexponentialSAT.lean.
A·f(n) < 1 compares only 2^(A·n·f(n)) with 2^n, not the complete bound C·(L+1)^d·2^(A·n·f(n)):
C, d and the encoding length L also decide any finite-instance conclusion.
log₁₀ n on a log axis (n from 10 to 10^(10⁷))
16/e² ≈ 2.1654, the max over real n ≥ 0, at n ≈ 5.1·10²³
peak of f itself, not of runtimeScale = n·f (which grows without bound)
Natural logarithms, as Real.log in the Lean; the +16 kept. Thresholds pinned at the integers in 60-digit decimal arithmetic;
for huge n, ln(n+16) is computed as x ln 10 + log1p(16·10^-x) with n = 10^x, never forming n itself.
The statement gives only A > 0 (and C, d, S, e > 0), all existential: the dashed lines are illustrations, not values from the paper.
Over integer n the maximum is f(514,843,556,263,457,213,182,250) = 16/e² − δ, δ ≈ 2.0·10^-54, a hair below.
Family 378, statement revision 7ef5c0cc5. Drawn by Fixpoint (eth_exponent_art.py).
